title: Element vs component: a description, not a call

slides.say: Component and element sound like the same thing. They're not, and the difference explains a lot about React.
A component is a function you write. It takes props and returns UI.
An element is what JSX creates: a small plain object. Its type is the Greeting function, and its props are the props you wrote.

slides.text: Creating an element does NOT call Greeting and creates no DOM. It's an instruction React reads later.
slides.say: Here's the key part. Creating the element doesn't run Greeting, and it doesn't touch the page. It's just an instruction that React reads later, when it renders.

slides.text: Elements are cheap and immutable: create them freely, never edit them.
slides.say: Elements are cheap, so don't try to avoid creating them. And treat them as read only. React even freezes them in development.
